title: Universal property of the henselization of a pair
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative ring, $J\subseteq B$ an ideal, and let $(B^h,J^h)$, $J^h=JB^h$, be the henselization of $(B,J)$ [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization], i.e. $B^h=\varinjlim_{C\in\mathcal C}C$ over the category $\mathcal C$ of etale $B$-algebras $C$ with $B/J\xrightarrow{\sim}C/JC$, and let $\eta:B\to B^h$ be its structure map (the coprojection of the object $\mathrm{id}_B$). Let $(A',I')$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and $\varphi:B\to A'$ a ring map with $\varphi(J)\subseteq I'$. Then there is exactly one ring map $\psi:B^h\to A'$ with $\psi\circ\eta=\varphi$; it satisfies $\psi(J^h)\subseteq I'$. (This is the clause 'left adjoint to the inclusion of henselian pairs into pairs' of Stacks 0A02, dropped from [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization] at its review.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization, line 2980), last paragraph of the proof ('Let $(A,I)\to(A',I')$ be a morphism of pairs with $(A',I')$ henselian. We will show there is a unique factorization $A\to A^h\to A'$ ...'): sections $\sigma_B:A'\otimes_AB\to A'$ by Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, (1)$\Rightarrow$(2)), their uniqueness by Algebra Lemma Tag 02FL (lemma-diagonal-unramified) and Lemma Tag 09XF (lemma-idempotents-determined-modulo-radical), then $\colim\sigma_B$; $\psi(J^h)\subseteq I'$ since $J^h=JB^h$

proof.text: *Set-up: $\eta$ and the coprojections.* View $A'$ as a $B$-algebra via $\varphi$. By [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization] (1) the category $\mathcal C$ is essentially small and filtered and $B^h=\varinjlim_{\mathcal C}C$ is the colimit in commutative $B$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with coprojections $\iota_C:C\to B^h$ ($B$-algebra maps, $\iota_{C_2}\circ\beta=\iota_{C_1}$ for every morphism $\beta:C_1\to C_2$ of $\mathcal C$); by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (1) $(B^h,(\iota_C))$ is also a colimit of the underlying diagram of commutative rings. $B$ with $\mathrm{id}_B$ is an object of $\mathcal C$: $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{id}_B)$ is an isomorphism, hence an open immersion, hence etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1), and $B/J\to B/J$ is the identity; $\eta=\iota_B$. For every object $C$ with structure map $u_C:B\to C$, $u_C$ is a $B$-algebra map, i.e. a morphism $B\to C$ of $\mathcal C$, so $\iota_C\circ u_C=\iota_B=\eta$ (cocone condition).

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization): 'It is nonempty because $\mathrm{id}:A\to A$ is an object', '$A^h=\colim_{B\in\mathcal C}B$'; the identification $\eta=\iota_B$ and the colimit of rings are implicit in Stacks

proof.text: *$(A',I')$: radical and Gabber's root condition.* Since $(A',I')$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-factorization-criterion] ($\Rightarrow$) gives (i) $I'$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $A'$, and (ii) every coprime monic factorization modulo $I'$ of a monic polynomial over $A'$ lifts to a factorization into monic polynomials. Gabber's root condition follows: let $h(T)=T^r(T-1)+c_rT^r+\dots+c_1T+c_0\in A'[T]$ with $r\ge1$ and $c_0,\dots,c_r\in I'$; then $h$ is monic and $\bar h=T^r\cdot(T-1)$ in $(A'/I')[T]$, with $T^r$, $T-1$ monic and generating the unit ideal ($1=T^r-(T-1)(T^{r-1}+\dots+T+1)$). By (ii) $h=gu$ with $g,u$ monic, $\bar g=T^r$, $\bar u=T-1$; $u$ is monic of degree $1$, so $u=T-\alpha$ with $\alpha\in1+I'$, and $h(\alpha)=g(\alpha)u(\alpha)=0$. So $(A',I')$ satisfies hypotheses (a) and (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-gabber-root-criterion-etale-section-lifting]. (This is Stacks' Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), (1)$\Rightarrow$(5), with the DAG's definition (09XI (3)) converted to (1) by [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-factorization-criterion]; the same argument is step 4 of [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-pair-approximation].)

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, line 2553), proof of (1)$\Rightarrow$(5): 'The factorization of $f \bmod I$ as $T^n$ times $T-1$ lifts to a factorization $f=gh$ ... $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical by the definition of a henselian pair'

proof.text: *The etale $A'$-algebras $C'$.* For an object $C$ of $\mathcal C$ put $C'=A'\otimes_BC$, an $A'$-algebra via $a'\mapsto a'\otimes1$, and $\kappa_C:C\to C'$, $c\mapsto1\otimes c$. Since $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is etale, $\operatorname{Spec}C'\to\operatorname{Spec}A'$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change]. Reduction modulo $I'$: as $\varphi(J)\subseteq I'$, $J$ acts by $0$ on $A'/I'$, so $C'/I'C'=(A'/I')\otimes_BC=(A'/I')\otimes_{B/J}(C/JC)$, and since $B/J\to C/JC$ is an isomorphism the map $A'/I'\to C'/I'C'$ is an isomorphism. Hence there is exactly one $A'$-algebra map $\rho_C:C'\to A'/I'$: existence, the quotient map followed by the inverse isomorphism; uniqueness, an $A'$-algebra map $C'\to A'/I'$ kills $I'C'$ and so factors through $C'/I'C'$, every element of which is the image of an element of $A'$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization, line 2980), last paragraph: 'for each $A\to B$ in $\mathcal C$ the ring map $A'\to B'=A'\otimes_AB$ is \'etale and induces an isomorphism $A'/I'\to B'/I'B'$'; the computation modulo $I'$ is written out by the agent

proof.text: *Existence of sections $\sigma_C$.* Let $C$ be an object and $\pi':A'\to A'/I'$ the quotient map. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-gabber-root-criterion-etale-section-lifting] to $(A',I')$ (hypotheses (a), (b) by step 2), the etale ring map $A'\to C'$ (step 3) and the $A'$-algebra map $\rho_C:C'\to A'/I'$ (step 3): there is an $A'$-algebra map $\sigma_C:C'\to A'$ with $\pi'\circ\sigma_C=\rho_C$, i.e. a section of $A'\to C'$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization, line 2980), last paragraph: 'Hence there is a section $\sigma_B:B'\to A'$ by Lemma \ref{lemma-characterize-henselian-pair}' (Tag 09XI, (1)$\Rightarrow$(2), here through (5)$\Rightarrow$(2))

proof.text: *Uniqueness of sections.* Let $C$ be an object and $\sigma,\sigma':C'\to A'$ two $A'$-algebra maps. Put $D=C'\otimes_{A'}C'$, a $C'$-algebra via $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and let $\mu:D\to C'$, $x\otimes y\mapsto xy$, a $C'$-algebra map. $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}C'$ is etale, as the base change of the etale $A'\to C'$ (step 3) along $A'\to C'$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change]; so by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-idempotent-splitting] (with $R=C'$, $S=D$, $s=\mu$) there is an idempotent $e\in D$ with $\mu(e)=1$ and $\ker\mu=(1-e)D$ (this is Algebra Lemma Tag 02FL, lemma-diagonal-unramified, for the etale map $A'\to C'$: $D=D_e\times(1-e)D$ with $D_e\cong C'$). Let $\theta:D\to A'$, $x\otimes y\mapsto\sigma(x)\sigma'(y)$, a ring map, and $f=\theta(1-e)$, an idempotent of $A'$. Both $\pi'\circ\sigma$ and $\pi'\circ\sigma'$ are $A'$-algebra maps $C'\to A'/I'$, so both equal $\rho_C$ (step 3); hence $\pi'\circ\theta=\pi'\circ\sigma\circ\mu$ (on $x\otimes y$: $\pi'\sigma(x)\,\pi'\sigma'(y)=\pi'\sigma(x)\,\pi'\sigma(y)=\pi'\sigma(xy)$), and $\pi'(f)=\pi'\sigma(\mu(1-e))=0$, i.e. $f\in I'$. The idempotents $f$ and $0$ of $A'$ differ by an element of $I'$, which lies in the Jacobson radical (step 2), so $f=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-idempotents-determined-modulo-radical] (Stacks: '$e=(\sigma_B\otimes\sigma_B')(0,1)$ is an idempotent contained in $I'$'). Hence $\theta(e)=1$ and $\theta$ kills $(1-e)D=\ker\mu$. For $x\in C'$, $x\otimes1-1\otimes x\in\ker\mu$, so $\sigma(x)-\sigma'(x)=\theta(x\otimes1-1\otimes x)=0$. Thus $\sigma_C$ is the unique $A'$-algebra map $C'\to A'$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization, line 2980), last paragraph: 'This follows once we prove that for every $B$ in $\mathcal C$ the section $\sigma_B$ is the unique $A'$-algebra map $B'\to A'$. We have $B'\otimes_{A'}B'=B'\times R$ for some ring $R$, see Algebra, Lemma 02FL ... We conclude that $e=0$ by Lemma 09XF'; the decomposition of $D$ is obtained from the section $\mu$ instead of Algebra Lemma Tag 02FL (algebra.tex line 41550), and $\sigma=\sigma'$ is deduced from $\theta(e)=1$ by the agent

proof.text: *Compatibility; existence of $\psi$.* For an object $C$ put $\psi_C=\sigma_C\circ\kappa_C:C\to A'$, a ring map; it is a $B$-algebra map, since $\kappa_C(u_C(b))=1\otimes u_C(b)=\varphi(b)\otimes1$ and $\sigma_C$ is $A'$-linear, so $\psi_C(u_C(b))=\varphi(b)$. Let $\beta:C_1\to C_2$ be a morphism of $\mathcal C$ and $\beta'=\mathrm{id}_{A'}\otimes\beta:C_1'\to C_2'$, an $A'$-algebra map with $\beta'\circ\kappa_{C_1}=\kappa_{C_2}\circ\beta$. Then $\sigma_{C_2}\circ\beta'$ is an $A'$-algebra map $C_1'\to A'$, so it equals $\sigma_{C_1}$ (step 5), and $\psi_{C_2}\circ\beta=\sigma_{C_2}\circ\beta'\circ\kappa_{C_1}=\psi_{C_1}$. So $(A',(\psi_C))$ is a cocone of $B$-algebras, and there is a $B$-algebra map $\psi:B^h\to A'$ with $\psi\circ\iota_C=\psi_C$ for all $C$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For $C=B$ (step 1), the map $m:B'=A'\otimes_BB\to A'$, $a'\otimes b\mapsto a'\varphi(b)$, is an $A'$-algebra map, so $\sigma_B=m$ (step 5) and $\psi\circ\eta=\psi\circ\iota_B=\psi_B=m\circ\kappa_B=\varphi$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization, line 2980), last paragraph: 'Given a morphism $B_1\to B_2$ in $\mathcal C$ we claim the diagram ... commutes ... Using the commutativity we obtain $A^h=\colim B\to\colim A'\otimes_AB\xrightarrow{\colim\sigma_B}A'$ as desired'

proof.text: *Uniqueness of $\psi$.* Let $\psi':B^h\to A'$ be a ring map with $\psi'\circ\eta=\varphi$. For an object $C$, $\chi_C=\psi'\circ\iota_C:C\to A'$ is a ring map with $\chi_C\circ u_C=\psi'\circ\eta=\varphi$ (step 1), i.e. a $B$-algebra map; by the universal property of the tensor product of commutative $B$-algebras there is an $A'$-algebra map $\tau_C:C'=A'\otimes_BC\to A'$, $a'\otimes c\mapsto a'\chi_C(c)$, with $\tau_C\circ\kappa_C=\chi_C$. By step 5, $\tau_C=\sigma_C$, so $\psi'\circ\iota_C=\psi_C=\psi\circ\iota_C$ for every object $C$. Since $B^h$ with the $\iota_C$ is a colimit of the diagram of commutative rings (step 1), the ring maps $\psi$ and $\psi'$ agreeing on all coprojections are equal [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization, line 2980), last paragraph: 'The uniqueness of the maps $\sigma_B$ also guarantees that this map is unique'; written out by the agent

proof.text: *$\psi(J^h)\subseteq I'$.* $J^h=JB^h$ consists of the sums $\sum_k\eta(j_k)x_k$ with $j_k\in J$, $x_k\in B^h$, and $\psi(\sum_k\eta(j_k)x_k)=\sum_k\varphi(j_k)\psi(x_k)\in I'$ because $\varphi(J)\subseteq I'$ and $I'$ is an ideal.

lean.statement: theorem henselization_universal_property (B : Type u) [CommRing B] (J : Ideal B) (c : Cocone (ObjectProperty.ι (fun C : Under (CommRingCat.of B) ↦ AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map C.hom) ∧ Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap (J.map C.hom.hom) C.hom.hom (Ideal.le_comap_map))))) (hc : Nonempty (IsColimit c)) (A' : Type u) [CommRing A'] (I' : Ideal A') [HenselianRing A' I'] (φ : B →+* A') (hφ : J.map φ ≤ I') : ∃ ψ : c.pt.right →+* A', RingHom.comp ψ (CommRingCat.Hom.hom c.pt.hom) = φ ∧ (J.map (CommRingCat.Hom.hom c.pt.hom)).map ψ ≤ I' ∧ ∀ ψ' : c.pt.right →+* A', RingHom.comp ψ' (CommRingCat.Hom.hom c.pt.hom) = φ → ψ' = ψ
